standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness up to a locally constant function for dimension functions, and the Cohen-Macaulay example
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Topology, label topology-lemma-dimension-function-unique (proof line 8313); Example example-CM-irreducible (proof line 8311)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the negative of the dimension of the local ring is a dimension function which vanishes at generic points, so that the relative dimension function differs from it by a locally constant function, giving the Cohen-Macaulay case.

core_obligations: Record the trivial implications and prove the converse: given the third condition, define the pieces as the sets of points with a fixed value, and note each piece is open because the union of the components through a point minus the union of those not through it is an open neighbourhood (proof lines 8299-8305).
Settle the normal case by the decomposition into integral schemes (proof lines 8305-8308).

Settle the Cohen-Macaulay case: the negative dimension of the local ring is a dimension function vanishing at generic points, and any two dimension functions differ by a locally constant function, so the second condition holds (proof lines 8309-8315).
proof_roadmap: Trivial implications and the converse (proof lines 8299-8305).
Cohen-Macaulay case via dimension functions (proof lines 8309-8315).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of three formulations of local equidimensionality for the relative dimension function, and shows that normal or Cohen-Macaulay schemes satisfy them (statement lines 8276-8297, tag 02RE-adjacent). The converse direction requires the observation that the set of points with a fixed value is open, and the two sufficient conditions come from the decomposition of a normal scheme into integral pieces and from the comparison of the relative dimension function with the dimension function given by local ring dimensions whose difference is locally constant. The openness argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
